review_notes: Read the whole file. The file's only simp-relevant declarations are the new def ψ and its two rfl unfolding lemmas. It has no @[simp] declarations of its own, and the [-simp] and [-instance] lists at the top only remove outside lemmas. I did not run Lean. The proposal is a moderate-confidence interface improvement. ψ is not reducible, so simp cannot unfold it. The three call sites already use an explicit rw chain that the lemma could replace. The cost is that other simp lemmas could change the resulting form, and I did not check that. Also, the file is a one-off solution file, so downstream benefit is limited.

findings.excerpt: theorem toMul_ψ_apply (Φ : NumberField.SIdele.obj E K S →+ Additive (AdeleRing (𝓞 K) K)ˣ) (x : NumberField.SIdele.obj E K S) :
findings.problem: ψ is a new noncomputable def, so simp does not unfold it. Its canonical evaluation lemma, toMul_ψ_apply, is a plain theorem with no @[simp]. Every use therefore spells out the rewrite by hand: `rw [toMul_ψ_apply, hequiv, toMul_ofMul, ...]` appears at lines 101, 142 and 162. Both unfolding lemmas (this one and ψ_apply) are also left unannotated. A user of ψ who calls simp gets stuck on `ψ Φ x` or `Additive.toMul (ψ Φ x)`.
findings.proposed_change: Mark toMul_ψ_apply as @[simp]. Its LHS `Additive.toMul (ψ Φ x)` has the head symbol ψ, and the RHS only uses the coercion to C K, so it cannot loop. Leave ψ_apply unannotated, or make it the simp lemma for the Additive-valued form, but not both. Both lemmas have the shape `ψ Φ x = ...` and would overlap when applied to the same term. The `rw [toMul_ψ_apply, ...]` steps could then be replaced by simp or simp only calls, with toMul_ofMul and toMul_zero already simp lemmas in Mathlib.
findings.benefit: The def gets a canonical evaluation rule. The three proofs of ψ_rho, ψ_eq_zero_iff and mem_range_ψ_iff no longer need to name the lemma. Later uses can reduce `ψ Φ x` to a class of a unit directly.
